title: Your First Night in the Grave

captions.tiktok: You will hear the footsteps of the people who buried you. Then the questions begin. Sahih al-Bukhari 1338.
captions.shorts: What happens on your first night in the grave, from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
captions.reels: You will hear the footsteps of the people who buried you. Then the questions begin. Sahih al-Bukhari 1338.

segments.text: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said that when you are laid in your grave and the people turn to leave... you hear them. You hear their footsteps, walking away.
And that is when your first night begins.
segments.title: THE FIRST NIGHT
segments.titleSub: what the Prophet taught about the grave

segments.text: Islam teaches that the grave is not empty waiting. Something happens there, and it happens to everyone. Two angels come to the one who has been buried... and sit them up.
And they ask about the man who brought the message. What did you use to say... about this man, Muhammad?

The believer answers plainly. I testify that he is the servant of Allah, and His messenger. Then he is told... look at your place in the Fire... Allah has exchanged it for a place in Paradise. And they will see both.

A longer account adds three questions. Who is your Lord. What is your religion. Who is this man. When the believer answers, a caller cries from heaven... My servant has spoken the truth. Spread for him a bed from Paradise... and open him a door to it.
And his grave is made wide... as far as his eye can see.

But the one who never really believed answers differently. I do not know... I used to say whatever the people used to say. For him, only the narrowing... and a blow that makes him cry out, heard by every creature nearby except humans and jinn.
segments.foot: Sahih al-Bukhari 1338; Sunan Abi Dawud 4753, graded sahih

segments.text: The Qur'an speaks to this night directly. Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word... in worldly life, and in the Hereafter. And the Prophet, peace be upon him, taught that this verse speaks of the grave.
One night. A few questions. And the strange mercy of it is that the questions are known in advance... every answer is being written by the way you live today.
